correspondence.component_scope: Chosen headward opening and long initial inland-ice passage
correspondence.finding: The chosen northern opening and the entire first southward passage fall in the national map's inland-ice area, west of the exposed coastal bedrock belt. The source depicts ice-surface and sub-ice thematic information here, not a named surface river.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper southwestward bend and ice-margin sequence
correspondence.finding: All short stored parts forming the upper southwestward bend are covered by the original map's continuous inland-ice and irregular exposed-rock-margin geography. Small mapped rock outcrops and the adjoining ice are visible throughout this section; none of these parts is omitted from the terrain correspondence.

correspondence.component_scope: Southern turn and eastward connector at the irregular ice/rock margin
correspondence.finding: The complete southward turn followed by the eastward connector lies within the readable ice-and-bedrock-margin setting. The source accounts for the whole connecting passage at regional scale without establishing a natural-river channel or a hydraulic link across it.

correspondence.component_scope: Southeastward intermediate sequence
correspondence.finding: The successive southeastward parts and their joins are covered by the mapped ice tongues, exposed-rock bodies and narrow intervening ice-margin terrain north of Hudson Land. The source shows the geographic setting continuously; it does not give a natural-river hydronym to this sequence.

correspondence.component_scope: Long lower southward passage and turn
correspondence.finding: The entire long lower southward section and its southern turn are visible in the original, in a mixed ice/bedrock-margin area on the northern side of Hudson Land. The selected line traverses the generalized mapped rock/ice setting rather than following a source-confirmed river trace. Its natural-river identity and continuity therefore remain unestablished.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower eastward sequence and actual selected terminal
correspondence.finding: All final eastward parts, including the last short bend and selected endpoint, are covered by the enlarged original coastal-margin cartography north of Hudson Land and west of Clavering Ø. The endpoint is in the generalized exposed-rock/ice-margin setting adjoining the western inner coastal inlet. This is not established as an ordinary river mouth, and the selected metadata's sea-terminal class is not treated as independent source proof. No exact modern shoreline or glacier-front position is claimed.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen opening across the ice-cap surface
correspondence.finding: The initial east-to-west bends lie within a continuous snow/ice-covered upland. Imagery locates the entire opening; it does not show these selected lines as a named open-water river. Ice-cap geographic correspondence does not establish a surface or subglacial hydraulic route.

correspondence.component_scope: Southwestward descent into an outlet-glacier valley
correspondence.finding: The selected corridor leaves the broad ice surface and descends along the eastern side of a large valley glacier between exposed rock ribs. All intervening stored parts are geographically covered. No lake passage or named river reach is established here.

correspondence.component_scope: Curving glacier trunk and transition to its outwash valley
correspondence.finding: The southward curving section follows the broad glacier tongue, including the junction with ice entering from the east, and reaches its lower outwash setting. The ice-to-outwash transition is visible at ordinary corridor scale; no precise modern ice-front boundary or meltwater conduit is assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Southward outwash river and western bend
correspondence.finding: A broad pale sediment-bearing fluvial corridor continues down the selected valley, narrows locally and turns around the western bend before returning southeast. Adjacent small lakes are off the selected corridor; none is promoted to a required through-lake connector. The intermediate joins remain within the same visibly continuous valley.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastward turn and eastern meltwater-river confluence
correspondence.finding: The northern outwash course turns east and meets a substantial stream arriving from the eastern glaciated valley, then turns south. The overview and lower detail show this ordinary connection. Historical primary prose independently describes the two southern/southwestern glacier-fed rivers converging toward the Kekertelung coastal setting; individual glacier-name assignment is withheld because its map was not observed.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower alluvial reach and actual selected endpoint
correspondence.finding: The final southwest-trending part and selected endpoint lie on the broad lower sediment-bearing river/alluvial corridor. In the imagery the endpoint is inland of the open coastal water, and the same visible channel continues southwest into coastal flats. CHS describes a large sediment-bearing river entering the channel northeast of Kekertelung Island. This locates the receiving setting without treating the selected endpoint as an exact surveyed coastline position or extending the selection.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected western opening and upper river
correspondence.finding: The selected opening lies on the mapped Barra Seca main valley along the São Gabriel da Palha–Nova Venécia boundary, rather than an unproven nearby headwater tributary. The upper river continues northeast and east past the Bonfim/Maruí/Santo Antônio tributary setting toward ES-137. The municipal original and study Figure2a show this connected upper course; no exact natural spring point is assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastward middle river and southeastern bend
correspondence.finding: The selected course follows the repeatedly labelled Rio Barra Seca east along the municipal boundary through the General Rondon, Sossego, Alegre, Jacarandá, São Jorge da Barra Seca and Jacutinga corridor, then bends southeast toward the Tesourinha/Jaguaré-side reach. The study distinguishes tributary mouths from the named receiving river; those tributaries are not selected branches or river aliases.

correspondence.component_scope: Sooretama margin to BR-101 and Macuco passage
correspondence.finding: The lower river proceeds southeast beside the northern margin of REBIO Sooretama, past the Paraisópolis and other tributary joins and the Barra Seca/BR-101 crossing. The same mapped river enters the broad Macuco wetland/lake reach, receives Cupido and continues east. The selected parts lie through that lake/wetland corridor; the lake name is retained separately from the river.

correspondence.component_scope: Southern wetland bend and Suruaca approach
correspondence.finding: The selected river follows the eastern forest-edge wetland south, passes the Pau Atravessado/Lagoa Bonita receiving setting and bends east into the Suruaca lowland. Jaguaré cartography depicts the river and lake/wetland corridor; the field study independently describes Barra Seca between Macuco and Suruaca with Pau Atravessado joining. Lagoa Bonita is a named joining waterbody, not an asserted traversal of its full north–south axis.

correspondence.component_scope: Suruaca to selected sea ending
correspondence.finding: The eastern selected part can be oriented from the Suruaca-side lowland toward the coast-parallel Barra Seca/Ipiranga setting. However, the final selected passage across the coastal strip into the Atlantic is not established by the read originals. The maps show longitudinal coastal water and a drainage/outlet connection farther north, while the study documents the distinct Barra Nova outlet and Suruaca–Ipiranga interventions. Those outlets are not substituted for the selected ending. This is a substantive missing through-link, not an exact-bank or present-flow requirement.

correspondence.component_scope: headward-opening
correspondence.finding: The chosen northwestern opening lies in a cultivated landscape with narrow linear drains and small depressions. The acquired imagery does not establish a named natural headwater or a continuous channel connecting every opening segment to the larger southeastern depression corridor. No nearby river or settlement label is substituted for that link.

correspondence.component_scope: upper-depression-chain
correspondence.finding: The selection runs along a broad southeast-trending belt of elongated depressions, irregular pale margins and scattered water surfaces within agricultural parcels. Ordinary landscape correspondence is visible; imagery alone does not establish the intervening transfers as one named arroyo, canal or lake passage.

correspondence.component_scope: middle-lowland-and-transport-crossing
correspondence.finding: The middle route alternates between elongated wet or pale low ground and cultivated intervals before crossing the east–west transport corridor. Huanchilla's planning report independently describes a flood-prone depressed plain and a proposed northern drainage intervention using existing railway and RP24 culverts. That local proposal does not demonstrate that these selected middle parts follow the proposed drain or any completed named canal.

correspondence.component_scope: south-central-field-transfers
correspondence.finding: South of the transport corridor, the route follows portions of low ground but also traverses intervening field blocks between dispersed water/depression features. No read source supplies the meaningful transfers connecting these features throughout the selected route.

correspondence.component_scope: lower-southern-loop-and-eastern-approach
correspondence.finding: The pronounced southern loop and subsequent eastward approach cross cultivated ground, scattered depressions and the margin of a broader wetland complex. Their through-connection cannot be established from this overview or from the bounded planning and field-study prose. A Canal Huanchilla or Canal Devoto identity is not assigned from proximity or administrative basin membership.

correspondence.component_scope: terminal-wetland-waterbody
correspondence.finding: The final short parts and ending occur in an extensive irregular waterbody and wetland/depression setting. Dark water surfaces and vegetated or exposed margins are visible in the terminal area. The waterbody's name, the full incoming connection and any onward receiving-channel identity remain unestablished; the model's endorheic classification is not independent hydrological proof.
